answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bound interaction bandwidth using transitive credit networks. Nodes record bilateral credit allowances in a trust atlas, routing transactions along funded paths across the peer nebula. An attacker cannot manufacture influence with virtual nodes, incurring the verifiable cost of locking scarce capital collateral into payment channels per identity. However, localized channel exhaustion can trigger a liquidity ripple, blocking honest agent traffic.
